learningObjectives: Distinguish Full Page, Partial, List and Form Views and their purposes
Configure a View for a Case Type Step in App Studio
Explain how Model-driven UI selects controls automatically from Field Types
Distinguish between Form Views and List Views and their editing behavior
Describe how Primary Fields on a data object propagate into Case Type Views

elements.description: A reusable configuration of UI elements used to capture or display data for a Case. Constellation applications are built on a View-based UI architecture (the Constellation Ruleset), and Views are reusable across Case Types.

elements.text: Views are like shared room plans: reference the same address layout in several places to avoid maintaining separate copies. The overall Case layout and the task’s input form have different roles.

elements.description: Constellation supplies reusable UI patterns and supported configuration choices. Its accessible defaults support implementation, but the finished application still needs accessibility testing.
Full Page supplies Case or data-object context; Partial presents read-only information; List presents collections; Form supports task input and can include read-only content.

elements.description: The UI layer follows the Separation of Concerns principle — the application is divided into distinct parts, each addressing one concern — so front-end components connect cleanly to back-end APIs.
Generated Views use templates for layout and responsiveness. Template options depend on View type and location; test the resulting application with the intended users and devices.

Auto-added per new Case Type/data object; the three-pane visual framework representing a single Case. Edited on the UX tab. While authoring, the Preview shows only placeholder text — run a Case instance to preview with real data.

The Summary panel sits upper-left and by default includes the Details View (showing Primary Fields) and Pulse View. A Promoted Action gives header access to a frequent Case-wide Action (e.g., Change Stage) — one per Case Type.

elements.description: Two ways: on the Workflow tab (configuring a Step's View auto-creates a Form View) or on the UX tab's Other Views pane. Form Views use the Default template; Step-associated Views can also use the Hierarchical template.

Set 1–3 columns; two-column is best practice. Narrow inputs (Text single line, Currency) take one column; wider/any-height inputs (Rich Text Editor, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Booleans, Attachments) span two columns, keeping tabbing left-to-right.

items: FIELD GROUP — clusters related fields under one header; specific to the View (not reusable)
MULTI-STEP FORM — one Assignment split across MULTIPLE Views (linear; default for Create Stage)
HIERARCHICAL FORM — one Form View divided into Form-group tabs; useful when users can complete groups in any order

elements.description: Each field has a name and a Field Type that determines its format/validation and the control shown. You configure field settings (label, required, visibility, etc.) to tailor capture and presentation.

Primary Fields identify important information and populate applicable standard Views, including Create, Edit, Details and List. A designation is not a required-field constraint; related data objects can supply their designated fields.

Field types and metadata determine the supported controls. Date fields use date input; Picklists support dropdown, search and radio presentation where appropriate. Model-driven does not mean every supported presentation is immutable.

Because controls derive from the model via reusable patterns, the UI stays consistent and responsive across devices/channels, and adapts automatically when rules change. You can still customize a control's presentation where needed.

elements.title: UI Design: Spot the Flaw

elements.description: A Portal is a web Channel. Configure its landing pages and navigation for its users; a task Form is a different interface within a Case. Responsive templates usually adapt the same UI to smaller screens.

Views present and collect information. Configure workflow processing with the appropriate Automations and Rules. Hiding a field does not authorize access, and client feedback does not replace server validation.

examPitfalls.title: View editability
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Read-only presentation and authorization are different concerns. Forms can include read-only content; a View setting is not a complete permission policy.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose the appropriate View type and supported editability; enforce permissions separately.

examPitfalls.title: Full Page View preview
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Authoring shows only placeholder text; run a Case to see real data. It is edited on the UX tab and is three-pane.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Placeholders at design time; run a Case instance for live data.

examPitfalls.title: One promoted Action per Case Type
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how many Actions can be promoted as the primary button on a Case page. Candidates say 'unlimited.' Only ONE Action per Case Type can be promoted — it appears as the primary button on the Case page header.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Exactly one promoted Action per Case Type; first Case-wide Action; no button component.

examPitfalls.title: Form View creation + default template
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Form configuration uses supported templates rather than an arbitrary blank canvas. Do not infer every template’s default column count from its name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Workflow tab + Step → Form View. Other templates come from creating other View types on the UX tab.

examPitfalls.title: Two-column layout and spanning inputs
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The prescribed two-column layout gives wider controls more space. Inspect the supported template behavior rather than assuming all inputs have the same width.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: One column: Text(single line), Currency. Span two: Rich Text Editor, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Booleans, Attachments.

examPitfalls.title: Model-driven control selection
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask why Pega automatically selects a Date control for a Date property. Candidates say the developer must manually assign control types. Pega uses model-driven UI — the property data type determines the default UI control automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set the right Field Type and the correct control renders automatically (date picker, checkbox, dropdown).

examPitfalls.title: Primary Fields and required fields
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Primary designations populate standard Views. They do not make a field required or move its data to the Case Type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure Primary and Required separately; inspect the applicable standard Views.

examPitfalls.title: Field groups and hierarchical Forms
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A hierarchical Form divides one Assignment into Form-group tabs. These groups are not independent reusable Views.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a reusable View for shared presentation, and keep hierarchical Form groups local to their Form.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A sales application must let customers use a self-service interface while employees use a work Portal. Where does an SA configure these application interfaces?

options.text: Channels — configure the interfaces through which different users interact with the application
Themes — changing colors creates a separate customer workflow and Portal menu
Case Life Cycle Stages — each Stage is a separate user interface channel
Data Pages — each data source defines a separate application interface

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider the entry point into the application, rather than its color scheme or data source.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Channels provide application interfaces. A Portal is a web Channel; its menu and content are configured for its users.

optionExplanations.A: Channels are the configuration entry point for application interfaces.
optionExplanations.B: Color changes do not create a separate Portal or workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Stages organize Case work, not application entry interfaces.
optionExplanations.D: A source of records is not the application interface configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to add a custom navigation tab labeled 'My Tasks' to the portal so all users see it immediately upon login. Where is this configuration made?

options.text: Portal configuration — add a landing page to Main navigation and configure the default landing page
Theme — change navigation colors and fonts to create a new menu item
Form View — add a field to a task form to create global Portal navigation
A Data Page — change the data source to add a Portal menu item

practiceQuiz.hint: Portal = navigation + global layout the user sees upon login.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configure the Portal menu and landing pages. Themes style the interface; task forms and data sources do not define its global menu.

optionExplanations.A: The Portal menu contains the landing pages available to its users.
optionExplanations.B: Styling a label does not add a navigation destination.
optionExplanations.C: Task fields belong to a form, not the Portal’s global menu.
optionExplanations.D: Fetching records cannot by itself add a Portal menu item.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A customer opens the same Constellation Lost Card form on a phone and a desktop browser. What normally adapts the form layout to the smaller screen?

options.text: Responsive View templates — the prescribed layout adjusts to the available screen width
A mobile-only Stage — duplicate the workflow Stage for every phone size
A new Case Type — duplicate the Case Type for every device breakpoint
A Data Page — the data source changes the screen dimensions

practiceQuiz.hint: Start with the responsive UI templates before creating a separate device-specific workflow.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Responsive templates adapt the existing interface. A smaller viewport does not inherently require a duplicate workflow or Case Type.

optionExplanations.A: The existing template can reflow at a smaller viewport.
optionExplanations.B: Duplicating workflow Stages by screen size mixes layout with process design.
optionExplanations.C: A viewport change does not require a new business Case Type.
optionExplanations.D: Data retrieval does not define the browser’s screen dimensions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA asks: 'What is the fundamental purpose of a View in Pega?' Which answer is correct?

options.text: A View defines the visual layout and the fields presented to a user within a UI screen or form
A View stores the business logic (validation, assignments) triggered when a user interacts with a field
A View is a Pega security artifact that controls which fields a user role can read or modify
A View caches the data displayed on a form so the screen loads without re-querying the data source

practiceQuiz.hint: A View = layout + fields shown to the user. Not logic, not security, not caching.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Views configure presentation and input. Routing, decisions and enforcement use the appropriate workflow and Rules; a View is neither a cache nor an access-control policy.

optionExplanations.A: A View defines how the relevant information is presented or collected.
optionExplanations.B: Routing and decisions need appropriate workflow or Rule configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Presentation is not a substitute for access-control rules.
optionExplanations.D: Caching belongs to the data-loading configuration, not the definition of a View.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Constellation form has a two-column grid. The grid contains: a single-line text field, a currency field, a rich text editor for comments, and a date picker. The designer asks: 'Which control breaks out of the two-column constraint and spans the full width?' Which is correct and why?

options.text: The Rich Text Editor spans both columns because it requires more vertical/horizontal space and is in the 'wider input' category that Constellation treats as full-width
The Currency field spans both columns because monetary values need wider formatting to display correctly in all locales
The Date picker spans both columns because it renders a calendar overlay that requires full-width positioning to display without clipping
All four fields follow the same two-column rule — none automatically spans both columns; width is configured manually for each field

practiceQuiz.hint: Which field type is in the 'any height, wider' category that makes it full-width?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Rich Text Editor (RTE) is in the 'any height / wider' category along with text areas, radio groups, checkboxes, attachments — these span both columns automatically in Constellation's two-column layout.

optionExplanations.A: The rich text input is a wider control in the prescribed two-column layout.
optionExplanations.B: A Currency input is not made full-width merely because it holds money.
optionExplanations.C: An overlay calendar is not the rule that determines this input span.
optionExplanations.D: The prescribed layout has different widths for different input types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is reviewing the default Views generated for a 'Loan Application' Case Type. A colleague asks: 'Which View is shown when a manager opens the Case to review it without editing any fields?' What is the answer?

options.text: The Full Page View — the Case framework containing read-only information and configured panels
The task Form View — the editable form for completing an Assignment
The Confirmation View — feedback after submitting an Assignment
The Portal landing page — a list or dashboard rather than the opened Case

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the overall Case interface from a task form.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Full Page View is the overall Case interface. Task Forms collect input; Confirmation follows submission.

optionExplanations.A: The Case framework gives context and displays the configured information.
optionExplanations.B: An editable task form has a different purpose from inspecting the Case.
optionExplanations.C: Confirmation is tied to submission, not a general Case inspection.
optionExplanations.D: A dashboard or list is not the individual Case interface in the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA adds a 'Submit' button to a form and observes that it triggers the next Case step and advances the workflow. What kind of element is this button within a View?

options.text: An Action — interactive controls such as Submit or Save that trigger business logic or workflow transitions
A Data element — the button stores a Boolean flag value that the Case engine reads to advance the workflow
A Section — a container grouping related fields; the Submit button is a specialized section boundary
A Channel — the Submit button is the channel-level trigger that signals the device to send the Case to the server

practiceQuiz.hint: Buttons that trigger logic = Actions in Pega's View anatomy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Submit button is an Action — an interactive control that triggers business logic or advances the workflow B is wrong because Data elements (properties) store field values — a button is not a data storage.

optionExplanations.A: Submitting invokes the task’s processing; the button is an interaction trigger.
optionExplanations.B: The button is not the stored Boolean property described here.
optionExplanations.C: A container groups UI content rather than submitting a task.
optionExplanations.D: A channel is an application interface, not an individual submit control.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA marks a field Required: Always in a Constellation form. A user leaves it empty while interacting with the form. Which behavior helps the user correct the missing value?

options.text: Client-side validation shows an inline required-field error associated with the field
A Channel replaces the Case workflow with another workflow
The Data Page automatically invents a valid value for the missing field
A Field Group bypasses all validation for its contained fields

practiceQuiz.hint: A required field should identify missing input, not silently manufacture a value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Required-field feedback identifies missing input. Server-side validation at submission remains necessary; client-side feedback does not replace it.

optionExplanations.A: Required-field feedback identifies the missing input next to the field.
optionExplanations.B: Switching workflows would not explain the missing required input.
optionExplanations.C: Inventing input silently would undermine the requirement to collect it.
optionExplanations.D: Grouping fields does not remove their validation constraints.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA opens a Case Type's Data Model in App Studio. She notices that 'Label' and 'Description' have a star/badge marking them as Primary. A junior BA asks: 'What does Primary mean here, and what happens automatically because of that designation?' What is the correct explanation?

options.text: Primary Fields are automatically included on the Create, Edit, and Details Views without any manual View configuration — marking a field Primary ensures it appears on standard Views without explicit placement
Primary Fields are mandatory (required) fields — marking a field Primary adds a required validation that prevents the Case from advancing if the field is empty
Primary Fields are displayed in the sidebar summary panel only — they appear as a quick-view list of key Case attributes without being on any editable form
Primary Fields are indexed in the Pega database for faster search — the designation improves query performance for Cases with many field properties

practiceQuiz.hint: Primary designation controls which Views auto-include the field without manual configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Primary Fields auto-appear on the Create, Edit, and Details Views — the key benefit is that those Views update automatically when you designate a field as Primary, without manual configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Primary designations reduce repeated configuration of standard Views.
optionExplanations.B: Primary and Required are different settings with different purposes.
optionExplanations.C: The designation also affects standard forms, not just a sidebar.
optionExplanations.D: Primary is a presentation designation, not a database-index request.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA configures Industry and Industry Subcategory picklists. The subcategory choices must depend on the selected Industry. Which model-driven pattern fits?

options.text: A cascading dropdown — pass the Industry value to the parameterized source for the Subcategory options
A theme change — colors filter which subcategories are available
A promoted Action — the Case header button replaces the dependent picklist source
A Ruleset version change — version numbers select the subcategory values

practiceQuiz.hint: The second field must use the first field value as an input to its choices.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Bind the dependent picklist source parameter to the selected Industry. Presentation colors and Rule version numbers are unrelated to that filtering.

optionExplanations.A: The second choice source receives the first field’s selected value.
optionExplanations.B: Colors do not constrain records returned for a dependent picklist.
optionExplanations.C: A header shortcut does not supply the picklist’s filtered options.
optionExplanations.D: Rule version numbers are not the business selection used by the filter.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During a design review an SA explains that Views should only define layout and field presentation, not business logic. A developer disagrees, saying the Submit button's action flow should be embedded in the View itself. Who is correct and why?

options.text: Keep presentation in Views and configure workflow processing with the appropriate Automations and Rules
The developer — embedding action flows in the View collocates the trigger and the logic, reducing configuration steps
Both — Pega allows business logic to be defined either in the View or in a separate Automation depending on complexity
Neither — business logic in Pega must always be defined in the Case Life Cycle Stage, not in Views or Automations

practiceQuiz.hint: Views = layout; Automations = business logic. Separation of concerns is a Pega SA principle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate workflow processing from layout. Views can configure field behavior, but a layout definition is not the container for the business workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Keep workflow behavior separately configured from its presentation.
optionExplanations.B: Putting the workflow definition inside a layout undermines maintainability.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario asks for separation, not an arbitrary choice of location.
optionExplanations.D: Logic can use suitable Rules and Automations beyond the Stage container.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA edits a Full Page View in App Studio and sees placeholder text. How should she inspect the UI with actual Case data?

options.text: Run a Case instance and inspect the rendered interface
Open the Application Layers Widget to populate the Case automatically
Toggle read-only mode to create live Case data
Change the theme to retrieve the last saved Case

practiceQuiz.hint: A configured layout needs an actual Case instance to show Case values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Full Page authoring preview uses placeholders. Running a Case supplies actual values; changing layout or theme does not.

optionExplanations.A: An actual Case supplies values that placeholder authoring lacks.
optionExplanations.B: The layers widget describes application composition, not Case values.
optionExplanations.C: Read-only controls alter editability; they do not create record data.
optionExplanations.D: A theme changes styling rather than selecting a saved Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA configures the View for a Collect information Step on the Workflow tab. Which View type does the system create?

options.text: A Form View for the Step, used to collect task data
A read-only Partial View as the Step’s standalone editing form
A List View that automatically completes every Assignment
A Portal landing page unrelated to the Step

practiceQuiz.hint: The task needs an input form.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Step configured from Workflow receives a task Form View. The overall Full Page View is a different container.

optionExplanations.A: The Workflow configuration creates the Form used by the user task.
optionExplanations.B: A read-only fragment cannot serve the editable role described.
optionExplanations.C: Displaying a collection does not complete the workflow automatically.
optionExplanations.D: The Step needs its task UI, not a separate Portal destination.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Constellation form, an upload field should be shown only when Attach supporting documents is selected. Which configuration fits?

options.text: A Visibility condition on the upload field, based on the checkbox value
A Channel that reroutes each checkbox click to another application
A submit Action that adds the upload field only after the form has closed
A Data Page that defines the complete form layout

practiceQuiz.hint: Configure the field’s conditional visibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Field visibility can depend on a condition. Hiding a field is presentation behavior, not an authorization boundary.

optionExplanations.A: The checkbox value is the input to the field’s Visibility condition.
optionExplanations.B: Rerouting to another interface is unnecessary for hiding one field.
optionExplanations.C: Showing the input only after submission misses the data-entry requirement.
optionExplanations.D: A Data Page provides records; it is not the definition of this form layout.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Shipping, Billing and Returns need the same address presentation in a Constellation application. Why embed a reusable Address View instead of copying the fields three times?

options.text: A shared View definition reduces duplicated presentation configuration and centralizes maintenance
Each embedding creates an unrelated permanent copy, so reuse has no maintenance benefit
Views cannot be reused across Case Types in the application
Embedding a View automatically doubles all server validation rules

practiceQuiz.hint: Use a shared presentation definition rather than independent copies.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A referenced View centralizes UI configuration. Independent copies diverge; reuse does not duplicate validation automatically.

optionExplanations.A: Referencing one View avoids maintaining three separate definitions.
optionExplanations.B: Independent copies describe copying, not referencing a shared View.
optionExplanations.C: Constellation supports reuse of Views across Case Types.
optionExplanations.D: Reuse does not automatically duplicate validation rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A designer asks how a Constellation form adapts to different screen sizes without creating a View for every breakpoint. What should the SA describe?

options.text: Constellation’s responsive templates and prescribed UI patterns
A manual Channel-to-pixel-width mapping for every screen resolution
A Data Page that decides browser viewport dimensions
Ruleset layering that assigns larger screens to higher layers

practiceQuiz.hint: Responsive layout is a UI template responsibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Responsive templates handle layout at different widths. Data sources and Ruleset precedence do not select layouts by screen size.

optionExplanations.A: Responsive UI patterns handle the same form at different widths.
optionExplanations.B: A separate mapping for each pixel width defeats responsive templates.
optionExplanations.C: A data payload does not determine the browser viewport.
optionExplanations.D: Ruleset precedence concerns Rule selection, not device dimensions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A product-category picklist must restrict the choices in a second product picklist. Which configuration sources the dependent choices from a Data Page?

options.text: Pass the selected category into the product Data Page parameter used by the second picklist
Embed every product permanently in the View definition regardless of category
Use a Channel to convert every character typed into a separate workflow Stage
Change the Case’s Ruleset version whenever the category changes

practiceQuiz.hint: Bind the source parameter to the earlier field.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The dependent choice source uses the selected category as a parameter. This avoids treating presentation definitions as a permanent product catalog.

optionExplanations.A: The earlier selection supplies the filter parameter for the dependent choices.
optionExplanations.B: A permanent unfiltered catalog in presentation does not meet the filtering requirement.
optionExplanations.C: Channels and Stages do not implement this dependent source relationship.
optionExplanations.D: Changing Rule versions is unrelated to the selected product category.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA's mentor reviews UI work and notes: 'You've placed assignment-advancing business logic inside a View. What should you do instead?' What is the correct approach?

options.text: Keep presentation in Views and configure workflow processing with the appropriate Automations and Rules
Keep it in the View but add a comment explaining why it is there, so future developers know it is intentional
Move it into the Data Page — Data Pages are the correct container for any logic that fires when a user submits a form
Duplicate it into both the View and an Automation so the logic runs regardless of which path the user takes

practiceQuiz.hint: Logic in a View → move to Automations. Views = presentation; Automations = logic.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate workflow processing from layout. Views can configure field behavior, but a layout definition is not the container for the business workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Keep workflow processing in the appropriate Automations and Rules.
optionExplanations.B: A comment does not remove the coupling between layout and workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Data sourcing is not a universal container for submit processing.
optionExplanations.D: Duplicating side effects risks executing the same work twice.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements distinguish the overall Constellation Case interface from the View for a user task?

options.text: The Full Page View provides the overall interface for an individual Case
Configuring a Step View from Workflow creates a Form View for that task
The Full Page View and task Form View have identical roles and configuration
A read-only Partial View is the editable top-level form generated for every Step

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate Case context from task input.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Full Page View provides Case context; the generated Step Form handles task data. Read-only Partials are reusable display fragments.

optionExplanations.A: Full Page supplies the context of the individual Case.
optionExplanations.B: The Step’s generated Form handles input for its task.
optionExplanations.C: Case context and task input are distinct responsibilities.
optionExplanations.D: A read-only Partial is not the generated editable task Form.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring UI controls for a new Case Type in App Studio. Which TWO statements are true about Model-driven UI in Pega Constellation?

options.text: Constellation selects the appropriate UI control automatically based on the field's data type
A Date field automatically renders as a date-picker control without manual configuration
Developers must manually assign a UI control to every field regardless of field type
Model-driven UI applies only to List Views and has no effect on Form Views

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what drives automatic control selection — field metadata, not manual configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Model-driven UI in Constellation reads each field's data type and metadata to automatically select the correct control — a Date field becomes a date-picker, a Boolean becomes a checkbox. Developers do not need to manually assign controls, and the behavior applies to both Form and List Views.

optionExplanations.A: Field metadata drives the set of appropriate UI controls.
optionExplanations.B: A Date field supplies the metadata for date-input presentation.
optionExplanations.C: Model-driven rendering avoids requiring a bespoke control for every field.
optionExplanations.D: The model also drives the controls on input Forms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business analyst asks how Form Views differ from List Views in a Pega Constellation application. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Form Views allow users to enter and edit field data for a single record
List Views display multiple records in a tabular or grid format
Form Views display multiple records side-by-side for comparison
List Views support full inline editing by default in Constellation

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall which view type is for single-record editing versus displaying a collection of records.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Forms collect task input. Lists present collections using the available templates; a read-only List must not be assumed editable without supported configuration.

optionExplanations.A: A Form supports collecting and editing the current task’s data.
optionExplanations.B: A List presents a collection rather than only one record’s input.
optionExplanations.C: Comparison of multiple records is not the defining purpose of a Form.
optionExplanations.D: Do not assume full inline editing on a default read-only List.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring Primary Fields on a Vehicle data object. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Primary Fields behave in Pega App Studio?

options.text: Primary Fields identify important descriptive fields on the data object
Designated Primary Fields automatically populate standard Views such as Create, Edit and Details
Primary Fields are required in every custom View regardless of task context
Making a field Primary moves its stored value from the data object onto the Case Type

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish automatic standard-View inclusion from a required field.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Primary is a presentation designation for important fields. It does not move data or impose required-field validation.

optionExplanations.A: Primary identifies important fields for routine presentation.
optionExplanations.B: The designation populates the applicable standard Views automatically.
optionExplanations.C: Important does not mean required in every custom task context.
optionExplanations.D: Presentation designation does not move the data to another object.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Constellation developer defines a Picklist field. Which TWO statements describe the relationship between the model and the control?

options.text: The field type determines the supported presentation choices
A Picklist can use dropdown, search or radio-button presentation as appropriate
Every field requires a manually coded UI component
Model-driven UI is limited to Data Pages and excludes Case fields

practiceQuiz.hint: Model-driven does not mean there is only one immutable presentation for every field.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The model constrains the available controls, while supported presentation choices remain configurable.

optionExplanations.A: The model determines which controls are suitable for the field.
optionExplanations.B: Supported choices can adapt the same Picklist to its usage.
optionExplanations.C: Model-driven authoring does not require a bespoke component per field.
optionExplanations.D: Case data fields also participate in model-driven presentation.

quickRecap.value: Full Page supplies Case context; Partial is read-only; List displays collections; Form handles task input and may contain read-only content.
Auto per Case/data object; three-pane; UX tab; Preview = placeholders, run a Case for real data.
Upper-left; Details (Primary Fields) + Pulse. Promoted Action: one per Case Type, first Case-wide Action, header button, no component.
Workflow Step configuration generates a Form. Templates control layout; hierarchical Form-group tabs belong to one Form and are not independent Views.
Auto on Create/Edit/Details; Label & Description default Primary on Case Types; reference fields inherit referenced object's Primary Fields.
Field types drive supported controls; Picklists can offer dropdown, search or radio presentation. Choose within supported options.
